title: Auditor DB credential sent over unauthenticated TLS (sslmode=require) and given in cleartext to any interceptor
description: scripts/lib/audit-database.mjs is the single transport for the CI auditor credential SUPABASE_TEST_AUDIT_DATABASE_URL, used by the check_realtime, check_data_quality, check_grants, check_deriva and check_phase3_audit gates and by atualizar-baseline. It accepts sslmode=require and passes it to psql as PGSSLMODE. Under require, libpq encrypts but does not authenticate the server when ~/.postgresql/root.crt is absent, which is the case on GitHub-hosted runners. It also sets no require_auth or channel_binding, so it answers whatever authentication method the peer asks for. An on-path or DNS-level attacker between the runner and db.gontnlfmothfglssbyyk.supabase.co (or the pooler) can present any certificate and request AuthenticationCleartextPassword, and receives the divat_auditor_ci password. Locally, the validated configuration sent a dummy password in cleartext to a loopback peer presenting a self-signed certificate for an unrelated name. The verify-full control sent nothing. docs/seguranca.md §9.5 records that the live secret currently depends on require. The sibling privileged path, scripts/backup_private.py, forces verify-full with system roots.
root_cause: SSLMODES_ACEITOS includes 'require' (and 'verify-ca'), and executarConsulta passes the chosen sslmode to libpq with no server-certificate verification and no PGREQUIREAUTH/PGCHANNELBINDING. The control that should bind the credential to the real server therefore fails open on certificate verification and on the authentication method.
intended_behavior: The auditor credential should only be released to a server that has proved it is the Supabase endpoint for gontnlfmothfglssbyyk: verify-full against a pinned Supabase CA. Password exposure should also be limited by refusing cleartext/MD5 auth (require_auth=scram-sha-256, ideally with channel_binding=require), matching the verify-full posture already enforced by scripts/backup_private.py.

trace.description: The secret SUPABASE_TEST_AUDIT_DATABASE_URL is injected into the gate environment. It is injected the same way at db-checks.yml:101 and :131, deriva.yml:64 and atualizar-baseline.yml:100.
The gate loads the credential through carregarConfiguracaoAuditora(). check_data_quality.mjs:85, check_deriva.mjs:95, check_grants.mjs:55 and check_phase3_audit.mjs:66 load it the same way.
Reads env[ENV_VAR] and passes it to validarConexaoAuditora.
Only checks that sslmode is in SSLMODES_ACEITOS (line 37: require, verify-ca, verify-full). 'require' passes without any root-certificate requirement.
Returns a frozen config that carries the password and sslmode='require'.

Spawns psql with PGPASSWORD (line 128) and PGSSLMODE=require, without PGSSLROOTCERT, PGREQUIREAUTH or PGCHANNELBINDING. libpq completes TLS with any server certificate and sends the password in cleartext when the peer requests it.

evidence.description: SSLMODES_ACEITOS = new Set(['require', 'verify-ca', 'verify-full']) — an unauthenticated TLS mode is accepted.
The module's security contract presents 'require' as acceptable TLS for the credential.
The test suite asserts that sslmode=require is accepted, so the fail-open mode is part of the guarded contract.

AUD-02 records that the validator accepts require 'que cifra sem conferir o certificado' and that the current secret would break the four mandatory checks if require were refused. The live secret therefore relies on require.
The sibling credential path forces PGSSLMODE=verify-full and PGSSLROOTCERT=system regardless of the URL. This is the stronger equivalent control the auditor path lacks.
Impact bound: the auditor login is asserted to have no direct table SELECT. What leaks is a minimal but persistent DB login to the shared database.

conditions.description: The SUPABASE_TEST_AUDIT_DATABASE_URL secret uses sslmode=require, which docs/seguranca.md:147-153 records as the current state (the secret value itself is not observable), and the runner has no ~/.postgresql/root.crt (default on GitHub-hosted runners).

The attacker can intercept or redirect TCP traffic, or DNS resolution, from a GitHub-hosted runner to db.gontnlfmothfglssbyyk.supabase.co or the Supabase pooler. The gates run daily and on every same-repo PR.
libpq (postgresql-client 16 on ubuntu-latest) has no require_auth or channel_binding set, so it answers an AuthenticationCleartextPassword request.

execution.attacker_perspective: An on-path network or DNS attacker between the CI runner and Supabase poses as the PostgreSQL server for db.gontnlfmothfglssbyyk.supabase.co, presents any self-signed certificate, and requests cleartext password authentication.
payloads: Fake server reply after SSLRequest: 'S'; after the TLS handshake (self-signed CN=attacker.invalid) and StartupMessage: AuthenticationCleartextPassword = b'R' + int32(8) + int32(3)
instructions: Inside the OS sandbox (uid 65534, no external network, isolated loopback only), generate a self-signed certificate for CN=attacker.invalid with openssl. Start scratch/fakepg.py on 127.0.0.1:54329; it answers SSLRequest with 'S', wraps TLS, requests AuthenticationCleartextPassword, records the PasswordMessage, then refuses the login.
Import the real validarConexaoAuditora/executarConsulta from scripts/lib/audit-database.mjs. Validate the payload URL and confirm it is accepted with sslmode=require.
Call executarConsulta with that validated config, changing only host/port to 127.0.0.1:54329 to stand in for DNS or route redirection of the real hostname, using psqlBin=/usr/bin/psql (16.15).
Repeat with sslmode=verify-full as a control.
execution.observed_result: A: the validator accepted host db.gontnlfmothfglssbyyk.supabase.co with sslmode=require. B: the fake peer logged tls_established TLSv1.3, startup_user divat_auditor_ci, client_msg_type 'p' and captured_cleartext_password 'DUMMY-AUDITOR-PW-A'; executarConsulta then threw AuditDatabaseError (status 2). C (verify-full control): the fake peer logged no_password_received after the client aborted TLS. Recorded in agents/h10-scripts/artifacts/check-01.out.

remediation.strategy: Accept only sslmode=verify-full, with a pinned, versioned Supabase CA certificate passed through PGSSLROOTCERT. Always set PGREQUIREAUTH=scram-sha-256, which stops cleartext/MD5 password disclosure even before the secret is rotated, and set PGCHANNELBINDING=require where the endpoint supports it. Reject libpq multi-host lists (',' in hostname). Rotate the divat_auditor_ci password after switching the secret. Regression tests: replace the 'require is accepted' loop in tests/audit-database.test.mjs with assertions that require and verify-ca are refused, that a comma host is refused, and that the env given to psql contains PGSSLMODE=verify-full, PGSSLROOTCERT and PGREQUIREAUTH=scram-sha-256. Add a loopback fake-server test like check-01 that asserts no PasswordMessage is sent to an unverified peer.

likelihood.reason: Requires an on-path or DNS-level position between a GitHub-hosted runner and Supabase. Such access is hard to obtain, although the credential is exercised daily and on every PR.

impact.reason: It exposes a protected CI secret, a persistent login to the shared production database valid until rotated. However, divat_auditor_ci is minimal: audit diagnostics and catalog reads, no table SELECT or writes. The gain is metadata disclosure and resource use within role limits.

confidence.reason: The fail-open transport is source-visible and was reproduced locally against the real module and psql 16.15, with a verify-full control. That the live secret uses require is taken from docs/seguranca.md:147-153 rather than observed.
